scrollField.inkFlipNote: Equal-contrast crossover (about 4.3:1 each) on the OKLab electric-to-day blend.

motion.name: reveal

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Hero photo entrance; the photo then holds still.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Hero copy and foot as the hero leaves; the photo stays.

motion.name: lit
motion.value: opacity 0.16->1, view() timeline, entry 100% to cover 50%
motion.purpose: How we work step-line words, one span each.

motion.name: trace
motion.value: scroll-drawn dash offset, rAF-throttled; pads fill 0.4s
motion.purpose: The circuit trace and its chip footprints.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: no reveal, lift, word light, settle or rise; trace fully drawn; field snaps; scroll-behavior auto

implementation: Scroll-driven animations are written as longhands (animation-name, animation-timing-function, animation-fill-mode, animation-timeline, animation-range); the minifier folds animation-timeline into the shorthand, which browsers reject.
One owner per transform channel: scroll lift on the hero copy wrapper's translate, load rise on its children's transform, settle on the inner photo's transform.
Trace geometry is read from offsetLeft/offsetTop, never getBoundingClientRect, so transforms from reveal animations do not move the route.
No CSS framework; a minimal reset lives in global.css.

signal.flip: swaps with the ink at field position 2.21, 0.6s ease

trace.start: chip lower-left edge mid-point, source pixel (857, 667) of 2000x1331, mapped through object-fit cover at 70% 50%
trace.routing: vertical and horizontal runs, 16px 45-degree corners; sideways jogs on one run 48px inside the top of the section entered; phone (<640px) first jog 24px below the chip; last leg arrives level with the pill

strokes.head: circle r 4.5, trace colour, at scrollY + 62% viewport

trace.pads: 22px SVG (16px under 40rem), 12px body + 12 pin stubs, 1.5px rule stroke, body fill var(--chip); .on fills with trace colour, 0.4s
trace.end: contact email pill gets outline 2px trace colour, offset 4px
trace.reducedMotion: fully drawn, head hidden, all pads lit

narrative.overview:
The page is a lit stage. One fixed colour field sits behind everything and carries the light: it holds midnight under the hero and How we work, flares once into electric cobalt for the proof in Featured work, and ends in daylight for Founders and Contact. Page surfaces are transparent so the field reads through every section. Nothing sits on a card. Depth comes from the field and from one real photograph, a processor held in tweezers, never from shadows or effects.

One circuit trace wires the page together. It leaves the chip in the photograph at its pins, routes down the page like a PCB track, passes a chip footprint at every step and section heading, and ends in the contact pill. Scroll draws it, and each footprint lights when the signal reaches it. Automation reads as one signal running from the problem to the contact.

There is one typeface, Familjen Grotesk, set heavy and tight at display sizes and plain at reading sizes. Each section holds a single idea at large scale, with a lot of air around it, so the page reads quickly and never gets dense. Acid lime is the one loud note. It goes on the actions, the signal, and a small number of words and figures, and it stays rare so it keeps its charge.

Motion is slow and tied to scroll: the hero photo settles in once; the hero copy lifts away as you leave while the chip stays, wired into the trace; the trace draws itself; step lines light word by word as you read; blocks ease in as they enter. The colour field and the trace are the signature interactions. Everything else stays still enough that the site feels light and fast.
keyCharacteristics: A single fixed scroll field of three colours (night, electric, day) across five sections is the only background; surfaces are transparent.
One scroll-drawn circuit trace runs from the hero chip to the contact pill, with square chip footprints at each heading.
Ink flips from light to dark at the equal-contrast point of the electric-to-day blend, and the signal flips from lime to cobalt with it.
Acid lime is reserved for pill fills, the signal, one key word or phrase, and the case figures.
One face, Familjen Grotesk, at weight 600 with negative tracking for display, and 400 for reading.
Every action is a full pill. There are no square buttons.
Imagery is real photography of technology, graded into the palette.
Hairline rules instead of cards. No shadows, glass, glow, or decorative gradients.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: The colour field is the only background. Sections, bars and blocks stay transparent. A new section adds a stop to the field. It never gets a painted panel.

rules.name: The Ink Flip Rule
rules.body: Ink flips from light (`fg-night`) to dark (`ink`) when the field position reaches 2.21, where both inks have equal contrast (about 4.3:1) on the OKLab electric-to-day blend. The flip toggles a day class on the root, which swaps text, secondary text, rules, accent, signal and footprint body together, and colour eases over 0.6s. When the field colours change, move the flip to the new contrast crossover.

rules.name: The Rare Lime Rule
rules.body: Lime is used for pill fills, the signal, the one key word of a headline, the one key phrase of a step line, and the hero numbers of proof, and nowhere else. Use one lime word or phrase per headline or step line at most. Lime text and lime strokes only go on night or electric grounds (5:1 or better). On day grounds lime is a pill fill with ink text only, because lime there measures 1.1:1; the signal turns Day Accent.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Familjen Grotesk is the only family. Build hierarchy from size, weight (400/500/600) and tracking. Text is balanced at headline sizes and pretty-wrapped in paragraphs.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Headings and figures at 1.75rem or larger are set at weight 600 with a line height of 1.05 or less and negative tracking that grows with size (-0.03em to -0.06em). The Step line is the one exception at weight 500 (1.05, -0.035em), because it is read as a sentence rather than scanned.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Don't use box-shadow, glass, backdrop blur, glow or decorative gradients. The only gradient allowed is a mask that feathers a photograph into the field.

rules.name: The Longhand Rule
rules.body: Write every scroll-driven animation as longhands (`animation-name`, `animation-timing-function`, `animation-fill-mode`, `animation-timeline`, `animation-range`), never the `animation` shorthand. The CSS minifier otherwise folds `animation-timeline` into the shorthand, which browsers reject, and the animation silently does nothing.

rules.name: The Split Transform Rule
rules.body: One element, one owner per transform channel. The scroll lift writes the individual `translate` property on the hero copy wrapper, the load rise writes `transform` on its children, and the settle owns the inner photo's `transform`, so no animation overwrites another. A new animation on an element that already moves takes a channel nobody else writes.

dos: **Do** put every background change on the single scroll field, as a new stop in section order.
**Do** flip the ink at the contrast crossover of the blend (currently position 2.21).
**Do** use a full pill for every action: lime fill with ink text for the primary, a hairline outline for the secondary.
**Do** limit lime to pill fills, the signal, one key headline word or step phrase, and proof figures. Use lime text and strokes only on night or electric grounds.
**Do** set display type in Familjen Grotesk 600 with tight negative tracking, and give each section one idea at large scale.
**Do** use real photography of technology, graded with the cobalt and lime ramps, or with the midnight duotone for people.
**Do** route a new section's heading onto the trace with a chip footprint at its first line, and jog sideways only inside the top of the section entered.
**Do** keep every target at least 2.75rem, and turn off all decorative motion under reduced motion.
**Do** write scroll-driven animations as longhands, and give each transform channel one owner.
donts: **Don't** bring back procedural 3D props or stages (rejected by the user).
**Don't** use glass, glow or blur effects, the "typical AI look" (rejected by the user).
**Don't** use flower or other non-tech imagery (rejected by the user).
**Don't** use square or square-cornered buttons (rejected by the user).
**Don't** set dense text. One idea per screen (rejected by the user).
**Don't** add heavy animation, WebGL, or an animation library. The site stays light and fast (user requirement).
**Don't** paint section backgrounds, cards or shadows. Surfaces stay transparent over the field; the chip footprints are the only filled shapes, and they belong to the trace.
**Don't** add a second typeface or set lime text on day grounds.
**Don't** invent figures. A lime number has to be a real one.
